jsDoc.doc:
A port to check availability of first. If the port isn't available, fall
back to another port.

Defaults to port 0, which will let the operating system choose an available
port.

Returns an available network port.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> In most cases, this function is not needed. Do not use it for trivial uses
> such as when using {@linkcode Ende.serve} or {@linkcode Ende.listen}
> directly. Instead, set the `port` option to `0` to automatically use an
> available port, then get the assigned port from the function's return
> object (see "Recommended Usage" example).

jsDoc.doc:
Parses a string as an IPv4 address.

The accepted syntax is the URL standard's
{@link https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-ipv4-address-string | valid IPv4-address string}:
four decimal octets separated by `.`, each written as the shortest possible
string of ASCII digits. Hexadecimal, octal and fewer-than-four-part forms are
rejected, as is surrounding whitespace.

tags.name: addr
tags.doc: IPv4 address in a string format (e.g., "192.168.0.1").

The four address bytes, or `undefined` if the string is not a valid
IPv4 address.

Parse an IPv4 address
```ts
import { parseIPv4 } from "@ende/net/unstable-ip"
import { assertEquals } from "@ende/assert"

assertEquals(parseIPv4("192.168.0.1"), new Uint8Array([192, 168, 0, 1]))
assertEquals(parseIPv4("0x7f.0.0.1"), undefined)
```

jsDoc.doc:
Validates whether a given string is a valid IPv4 address.

See {@linkcode parseIPv4} for the accepted syntax.

tags.name: addr
tags.doc: IPv4 address in a string format (e.g., "192.168.0.1").
A boolean indicating if the string is a valid IPv4 address.

Check if the address is a IPv4
```ts
import { isIPv4 } from "@ende/net/unstable-ip"
import { assert, assertFalse } from "@ende/assert"

const correctIp = "192.168.0.1"
const incorrectIp = "192.168.0.256"

assert(isIPv4(correctIp))
assertFalse(isIPv4(incorrectIp))
```

jsDoc.doc:
Parses a string as an IPv6 address.

Implements the URL standard's
{@link https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-ipv6-parser | IPv6 parser}, which
covers `::` compression and the trailing `x:x:x:x:x:x:d.d.d.d` form. Zone
IDs (`fe80::1%eth0`) are intentionally omitted by that standard and are
rejected here too, unlike `node:net`'s `isIP()`.

tags.name: addr
tags.doc: IPv6 address in a string format (e.g., "2001:db8::1").

The sixteen address bytes, or `undefined` if the string is not a
valid IPv6 address.

Parse an IPv6 address
```ts
import { parseIPv6 } from "@ende/net/unstable-ip"
import { assertEquals } from "@ende/assert"

const loopback = new Uint8Array(16)
loopback[15] = 1

assertEquals(parseIPv6("::1"), loopback)
assertEquals(parseIPv6("2001:db8:::1"), undefined)
```

tags.name: addr

import { isIPv6 } from "@ende/net/unstable-ip"

const correctIp = "2001::db8:0:1"
